task: Ask what Rafi should bring to soccer practice tomorrow, then ask a follow-up in the same conversation (what time it starts and where). Then, separately, ask the app to plan dinners this week, and after that ask whether Rafi's school bus runs on snow days. If the app ever looks like it handed a question to the wrong place, fix that yourself in the app.
transcript: Opened the app: a Home screen saying 'What can I help with?', three example prompts, a text box and Send, plus a reassurance that nothing is sent without my OK.
Typed 'What should Rafi bring to soccer practice tomorrow?' and tapped Send; the button showed 'Sending'.
After 30s the conversation opened, titled 'Find out what Rafi needs for practice', with 'Your family admin helper is on it', Change and Details links, and 'Working on it'.

After another 30s the answer came: the coach sent no list, practice is Sat Nov 14 9:00-10:30 at Riverside Park field 3, bring cleats, shin guards, water, a warm layer, maybe a ball; offered to write a note to the coach.
Typed the follow-up 'what time does it start and where is it?' in the 'Reply or ask a follow-up' box and tapped Send.
Waited about 2.5 minutes of 'Working on it' (it showed '1 min' while waiting) before the answer came.
Answer: practice starts 9:00am tomorrow, Sat Nov 14, at Riverside Park field 3, ends 10:30. Same conversation, consistent with the first answer.

Scrolled up and tapped 'All' once with no visible change, then tapped '‹ All' and got a list of my conversations, including older ones about an FSA amount and Ezra's Hudson Prep application whose previews start with 'STATUS:'.
From the list I typed 'Can you plan dinners for this week?' and tapped Send; a new conversation 'Plan this week's dinners' opened.

Within about 30-60s it gave dinners Fri Nov 13 to Thu Nov 19 using my CSA box, working around a dentist day, conference sign-ups at 7 Sunday, and Noa's 6pm recital Wednesday, with a short shopping list and an offer for a full grocery list.
Went back with '‹ All'; the list now also showed 'Keep Rafi's reading on track' and 'Stay ahead of the family calendar' as 'Working on it', which I had not asked for just now.
Typed 'Does Rafi's school bus run on snow days?' and tapped Send; a new conversation 'Check whether Rafi's bus runs on snow days' opened with the family admin helper on it.

After about 1.5-2 minutes it said it found nothing about the bus or snow days in my email, explained schools usually post closures, and showed an unsent draft email to Ms. Ortiz at Maple with 'Open in Mail' and 'Copy' buttons.
Nothing looked like it went to the wrong place, so I did not use Change.
stumbles: The simple follow-up about time and place took about 2.5 minutes even though the first answer already said 9:00 at Riverside Park field 3.
The way back to the conversation list is a small '‹ All' at the top that scrolls off once a conversation is long; I had to scroll up and my first tap on 'All' did nothing visible.
Asking something new from the list screen reuses the 'Reply or ask a follow-up' box, so I was not sure whether it would land in an old conversation (it correctly started a new one).
Older conversations in the list show previews that start with 'STATUS:', which reads like a system label.
Two items I had not just asked for ('Keep Rafi's reading on track', 'Stay ahead of the family calendar') appeared as 'Working on it' in the list, which was a little surprising.
verdict: All four questions got correct, useful answers in the right place: the follow-up stayed in the soccer conversation, dinners and the bus question each got their own, and the bus answer honestly said it did not know and offered an unsent draft. It felt close to ChatGPT, held back mainly by the slow follow-up, the small back link, and a 'STATUS:' label in the list.
